claims: Theorem 1 (README, note draft v0.6 of 2026-10-13, not in the repository): s(n^2 - n + 1) < n for every integer n >= 15.

Theorem 2: for n >= 15 and integers p, q >= 0 with 16p + 21q <= n - 15, n^2 - n + 1 + p + 2q unit squares pack in a square of side less than n; in particular s(n^2 - n + F(n)) < n with F(n) = 1 + max{p + 2q : 16p + 21q <= n - 15}.

Lemma 3 (tools/glue.py): a rectangle packing A in an a x b box (a > b) squeezed by d_A and a square packing B in an m x m box squeezed by d_B glue with two integer blocks into n^2 - waste_A - waste_B squares in side n - d, n = b + m, d = min(d_A, d_B, 1/2).

Proposition 4: R, 257 squares in (17 - delta) x (16 - delta), delta >= 7.436e-4 (rectangles/r17x16_n0257); and R', 443 squares in (22 - d) x (21 - d), d >= 0.0094, waste 19 (rectangles/r22x21_n0443), with four further rectangles of waste b - 1.

theorem/: for every n = 15..64, an exact strict certificate of n^2 - n + F(n) unit squares in a square of side n - 1/20000, built by the uniform construction at squeeze 1/10000, counts 211 to 4037; and 26 best-excess certificates in theorem/best/ at the same side, counts 308 to 4038.

composites/: the 230 Section 5 composites of draft v0.3, the best j for 27 <= n <= 64 shipped as 38 certificates, all regenerated bit for bit by composites/reproduce.sh; dominated in excess at every n by theorem/best.tsv.
VERIFICATION.md: all 76 theorem certificates pass squarepack.verify --strict, tools/rectcheck.py and Daniel's verify_cert.py; failures 0.
